key_genomic_segments: Standard-risk cytogenetics: ~60-65% NDMM (t(11;14), hyperdiploid, no high-risk lesion)

del(17p) / TP53 loss: ~10% NDMM, ~30% in late-line
Extramedullary disease (EMD): ~5-15% at dx, ~30% at relapse
Plasma cell leukaemia (PCL): <5% — most aggressive variant
Penta-refractory MM: refractory to 2+ PIs, 2+ IMiDs, anti-CD38

competitive_dynamics.belantamab_schedule_optimisation_note: Belantamab mafodotin Part 2 dosing schedule (ASCO 2026 NDMM combination cohort, NCT04091126) eliminates Grade ≥3 keratopathy (0% Part 2 vs 0.6% Part 1) and reduces Grade ≥2 keratopathy to 6.7-10.6% of assessments. Combined with the DREAMM-7 and DREAMM-8 commercial relistings (2025) and the DREAMM-10 NDMM combination programme, the keratopathy overhang that drove the 2022 US withdrawal is now substantially mitigated for combination regimens. Strategic implication: belantamab is no longer toxicity-disadvantaged vs BCMA bispecifics in the combination setting; competition shifts to durability, sequencing, and commercial terms

access_economics_axis.summary: Cost-effectiveness / access is now a distinct competitive lever in BCMA bispecific-vs-CAR-T positioning (alongside efficacy, safety, sequencing). ASCO 2026 teclistamab + daratumumab cost-effectiveness analysis: ICER $82,074/QALY vs $150,000/QALY WTP threshold; 88.9% of PSA simulations favour tec+dara at the $150K threshold; total lifetime cost $445K (tec+dara) vs $350K (DPd/DVd). Framed against the 'CAR-T premium' (apheresis bottleneck, manufacturing cost, bridging therapy), bispecifics carry an access-economics advantage in the broader-uptake setting

review_framing_notes.mrna_cart_third_bcma_class: Per NRDD 2026 (Chien et al., DOI 10.1038/s41573-026-01459-7) the BCMA-CAR-T competitive map in MM now spans three classes: (1) lentiviral autologous CAR-T (ide-cel, cilta-cel) — durable but requires lymphodepletion + ICU-adjacent monitoring; (2) BCMA bispecifics (teclistamab, elranatamab) — off-the-shelf; (3) mRNA-encoded CAR-T (Cartesian's Descartes-15) — transient, no-preconditioning, outpatient-friendly, repeat-dose feasible. The bet is that transient-but-repeatable yields a different risk/benefit profile that could shift earlier-line use. Cross-platform readacross: Descartes-08 reportedly showed ~83% month-12 response in gMG (Ph2b) despite transient CAR expression
review_framing_notes.proteasome_inhibition_vs_targeted_degrad: Conceptual framing (Nat Rev Cancer 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41568-025-00817-8): MM SOC PIs (bortezomib/carfilzomib/ixazomib) BLOCK the proteasome broadly (stabilising tumour-suppressors), whereas TPD (IMiDs/CELMoDs/PROTACs) REPROGRAMMES the UPS to selectively destroy oncoproteins. The review positions these as complementary — giving next-gen MGD + PI combinations a mechanistic rationale beyond empirical synergy. [framing only]
review_framing_notes.cd38_rlt_cross_modality_readacross: RLT modality umbrella review (NRDD, DOI 10.1038/d41573-025-00096-w, Fig 2b) shows clinical-stage radioligand-therapy activity at CD38 — the same validated MM target as daratumumab/isatuximab (antibody class) — i.e. cross-modality redeployment of a validated MM target into an RLT format. Asset-level details (sponsor, INN, NCT) NOT provided by the review; no asset added to pipeline_assets to avoid fabrication. [framing only]

competitive_dynamics.frontline_trispecific_wave_note: Watch signal (2026-07-23; zero-efficacy, context only -- no benchmark write). A frontline/earlier-line TRIspecific wave is emerging in MM: (1) ramantamig (BCMA x GPRC5D x CD3 trispecific) + daratumumab enters 1L NDMM non-transplant via TRIlogy-7 (NCT07665450, NOT_YET_RECRUITING, no efficacy yet) -- the first trispecific to target 1L NDMM; (2) IBI3003 (GPRC5D x BCMA x CD3 trispecific, Innovent) is now in Phase 3 RRMM. Two assets make this a class-wide trend rather than a single-asset outlier: a dual-antigen-escape trispecific could challenge the quadruplet-backbone (IMiD/PI/CD38) frontline narrative IF efficacy lands. Per standing policy this does NOT displace the quadruplet benchmark anchors (IMROZ Isa-VRd, CEPHEUS Dara-VRd ORR 91%, MAIA D-Rd 61.9mo) on zero-efficacy trial-starts -- reassess at first efficacy readout

wuxi_coins_act_2026.summary: BIOSECURE Act enacted 2025-12-18 as FY2026 NDAA section 851. WuXi AppTec added to the DoD section 1260H list 2026-06-08 (188 entities). This creates active, 1260H-linked BIOSECURE/federal-contracting exposure for US biopharma partnerships relying on WuXi AppTec — NOT a proposed-only bill, NOT a sanctions designation, and NOT a blanket commercial ban
wuxi_coins_act_2026.mm_relevance: WuXi AppTec is a contract-research/manufacturing partner used across MM developer programmes (small-molecule and biologics CDMO/CRO services). 1260H listing + enacted BIOSECURE raises federal-contracting and supply-chain-continuity diligence for MM sponsors that rely on WuXi capacity; monitor for contract-rebalancing and dual-sourcing in MM pipeline programmes
wuxi_coins_act_2026.coins_act_note: Separately, a US House bill proposes extending the COINS Act outbound-investment review to biotechnology following recent large pharma-China deals — this COINS extension remains PROPOSED (distinct from the enacted BIOSECURE/1260H exposure above) and stays categorical-HR until enactment

regulatory_landscape.talquetamab_2L_label_expansion_priority_: FDA granted priority review (2026-05-15) for talquetamab (Talvey, GPRC5D×CD3) label expansion from 4L+ to 2L+ in RRMM, based on MonumenTAL efficacy-extension data. A 2L+ label would roughly double the US addressable population and could displace PI-IMiD-CD38 triplet retreatment in 2L; timing ahead of MonumenTAL-3 Ph3 readout gives Janssen early earlier-line bispecific positioning. Sources: J&J/Janssen PR 2026-05-15
